newsitem.title: USA: CUC to acquire Hebdo Mag in $440 million stock swap.
newsitem.headline: CUC to acquire Hebdo Mag in $440 million stock swap.

text.p: CUC International Inc., seeking to extend its reach in global online commerce, said Thursday it agreed to acquire Paris-based classified advertising publisher Hebdo Mag International in a stock swap worth $440 million.

CUC International is a consumer services company that provides access to travel, shopping, auto, dining, financial, and other services to more than 68 million consumers worldwide through more than 20 membership programs.

"This is a good strategic fit as classified advertisements are integral to our goal of reaching consumers just before every significant purchasing decision they make," CUC Chairman Walter Forbes said in a statement.

Hebdo Mag is jointly owned by founders Louise and John MacBain and Canada's Torstar Corp., publisher of the Toronto Star. Both the MacBains and Torstar will sell their stakes in Hebdo to CUC, but the MacBains will continue to manage the business on a day-to-day basis, CUC said.
The acquisition of Hebdo Mag comes as CUC prepares to close an $11 billion merger with HFS Inc., a rapidly expanding real estate and travel services company.

"With CUC's existing consumer services and HFS's preferred alliances, we will now be able to leverage our direct-marketing expertise to cross-sell complementary services, such as AutoVantage, to someone buying a car," CUC's Forbes said.

Hebdo Mag has operations in 12 countries, including Canada, France, Sweden, Hungary, the United States, Italy, Russia, and Holland. The company publishes over 150 titles in 12 countries on 3 continents.
CUC markets items ranging from educational and entertainment software to a full-service travel agency to the Welcome Wagon and Entertainment coupon books.

CUC said it intends to account for the acquisition of privately held Hebdo Mag as a pooling of interests. The deal, which CUC said will give a slight boost to its 1997 earnings, is expected to close in October.
In its fiscal year ended January 31, 1997, Stamford, Conn.-based CUC earned $164.1 million on revenues of $2.3 billion.
Hebdo Mag expects to post revenues for 1997 of $200 million and $60 million in earnings before income taxes, depreciation and amortization, CUC said.
CUC stock fell 6 cents to $26.44 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
